gaps: The case names QA vendor 3, but the vocabulary supports only the invited QA vendor and QA vendor 2; the plan uses vendor2.
The available tokens do not expose QA vendor 1's submitted price, so the plan cannot guarantee that 200 is higher than that bid.
the decisive step tests something else than the case's point: No supported read-back field directly verifies the unchanged L1 value; the comparison rank is verified instead.

words.preconditions: A fresh published RFQ event where the invited QA vendor has submitted a bid; bidding still open.
steps: The buyer invites QA vendor 2 to the live pricing round.
The buyer enters a surrogate bid of 200 on the vendor's behalf for a second QA vendor.
As the buyer, read the pricing round and check that Data check: “bid count” equals 2.

As the buyer, read the round's comparison (ranks, best bidder) and check that Data check: “auction identifiers data › QA vendor 1 › inline › the line › rank” equals 1; Data check: “auction identifiers data › QA vendor 2 › inline › the line › rank” is at least 2.
words.expected: The app accepts it. Read back afterwards: Data check: “bid count” equals 2; Data check: “auction identifiers data › QA vendor 1 › inline › the line › rank” equals 1; Data check: “auction identifiers data › QA vendor 2 › inline › the line › rank” is at least 2.
